# Code

```{r}

## =============================================================================
## IDEA-RS temporal external validation in the 2004 Pelotas Birth Cohort
##
## Reproduces the analyses reported in the manuscript: exclusion cascade, Tables
## 1-2, Figures 2-3, sensitivity analyses, attrition and missingness analyses,
## and Supplementary Tables S3-S10 and Figures S1-S5.
##
## Inputs (in data/):
##   Banco_IDEA_RS_idalt.dta
##   Banco_IDEA_RS_idalt2.dta
##   pelotas_2004_com_mania_raw.dta
##
## Outputs:
##   results/       figures (.png) and one Excel workbook with all tables
##   data/derived/  analytic datasets (.csv)
##
## Paths are relative to the folder containing this file. Quarto sets this
## automatically; when running interactively, set the working directory to that
## folder.
## =============================================================================

## ---- 1. Setup ---------------------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(haven)
library(labelled)
library(readr)
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(pROC)
library(patchwork)
library(openxlsx)
library(WeightedROC)

set.seed(2024)
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("data/derived", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

## Colour used for the ROC curve and all calibration plots.
PLOT_BLUE <- "blue"

## Number of bootstrap replicates used throughout.
N_BOOT <- 2000

## ---- 2. Load raw data --------------------------------------------------------

pelotas_2004_raw           <- read_dta("data/Banco_IDEA_RS_idalt.dta") %>% remove_var_label()
pelotas_2004_com_mania_raw <- read_dta("data/pelotas_2004_com_mania_raw.dta") %>% remove_var_label()
## Supplementary extract: IQ (age 6), SDQ (ages 11 and 15, parent-report), DAWBA
## (age 11), and maternal education and household income at birth.
pelotas_2004_extra_raw     <- read_dta("data/Banco_IDEA_RS_idalt2.dta") %>% remove_var_label()

n_raw <- nrow(pelotas_2004_raw)
cat(sprintf("Enrolled at birth: N = %d\n", n_raw))

## jsmba6 (age-18 depression outcome) is kept out of predictor_15y_vars so that
## completeness of the age-15 predictors can be assessed independently of
## outcome availability.

predictor_15y_vars <- c(
  "asexo","acorpele",
  "dcmadep","dcotdep","dcundif","icmadep","icotdep","icundif",
  "hconff109","hconff110","hconff111","hconff112","hconff113","hconff114","hconff115",
  "hconfb10a","hconfb10b","hconfb10c","hconfb10d","hconfb10f",
  "hgh98","hgf58","hcmc38","hconfc48","hconfc49","hconfc51","hconfc53"
)

## Labels for the raw variable codes, used to report missingness per derived
## predictor or questionnaire module (Table S4). The six DAWBA fields define the
## baseline-depression exclusion and are not IDEA-RS predictors. The seven
## maltreatment items and five drug-use items are each summed into one derived
## predictor, so each group is reported as a single row.
predictor_15y_var_groups <- c(
  asexo = "Sex", acorpele = "Skin colour",
  dcmadep = "Baseline depression screen (DAWBA) — exclusion criterion, not an IDEA-RS predictor",
  dcotdep = "Baseline depression screen (DAWBA) — exclusion criterion, not an IDEA-RS predictor",
  dcundif = "Baseline depression screen (DAWBA) — exclusion criterion, not an IDEA-RS predictor",
  icmadep = "Baseline depression screen (DAWBA) — exclusion criterion, not an IDEA-RS predictor",
  icotdep = "Baseline depression screen (DAWBA) — exclusion criterion, not an IDEA-RS predictor",
  icundif = "Baseline depression screen (DAWBA) — exclusion criterion, not an IDEA-RS predictor",
  hconff109 = "Childhood maltreatment", hconff110 = "Childhood maltreatment",
  hconff111 = "Childhood maltreatment", hconff112 = "Childhood maltreatment",
  hconff113 = "Childhood maltreatment", hconff114 = "Childhood maltreatment",
  hconff115 = "Childhood maltreatment",
  hconfb10a = "Any drug use", hconfb10b = "Any drug use", hconfb10c = "Any drug use",
  hconfb10d = "Any drug use", hconfb10f = "Any drug use",
  hgh98 = "School failure", hgf58 = "Social isolation", hcmc38 = "Fight involvement",
  hconfc48 = "Ran away from home", hconfc49 = "Relationship with father",
  hconfc51 = "Relationship with mother", hconfc53 = "Relationship between parents"
)
stopifnot(all(predictor_15y_vars %in% names(predictor_15y_var_groups)))

core_vars <- c("idalt20241223", predictor_15y_vars, "jsmba6")

## ---- 3. Puberty and mania status (merged onto every enrolled participant) ----

puberty_boys <- pelotas_2004_raw %>%
  filter(asexo == 1) %>%
  transmute(idalt20241223,
            puberty_data_present = !is.na(hconfmasce87) | !is.na(hconfmasce88),
            puberty_started = (hconfmasce87 > 1 | hconfmasce88 > 1))

puberty_girls <- pelotas_2004_raw %>%
  filter(asexo == 2) %>%
  transmute(idalt20241223,
            puberty_data_present = !is.na(hconffeme87) | !is.na(hconffeme88),
            puberty_started = (hconffeme87 > 1 | hconffeme88 > 1))

puberty_status <- bind_rows(puberty_boys, puberty_girls)

## jsmbb8/jsmbb9: manic/hypomanic episode flags from the MINI algorithm
## (standard, not duration-corrected), ascertained at the age-18 interview.
mania_status <- pelotas_2004_com_mania_raw %>%
  transmute(idalt20241223,
            mania_data_present = !is.na(jsmbb3),
            ever_manic_hypomanic = (jsmbb8 == 1 | jsmbb9 == 1))

## ---- 4. Main-analysis eligibility cascade -----------------------------------
## Sequence: complete age-15 predictors -> no baseline (age-15) depression ->
## puberty -> age-18 outcome available -> mania screening data available.
## Lifetime mania/hypomania does not reduce N: these participants are retained
## and recoded as non-cases (Section 8).
##
## eligibility_group separates exclusions by design (pre-pubertal or ambiguous
## puberty status, baseline depression) from missing data (incomplete age-15
## predictors, missing puberty data, missing age-18 outcome, missing mania
## screen). It is used in Section 7B and in the IPW models.

## DAWBA fields (age 15: dc*/ic*; age 11: gdc*/gic*) are scored positive if
## they are not 0. Values are checked against the observed banding (0-4), so an
## unexpected code (e.g. a negative sentinel, which would read as positive)
## fails loudly.
dawba_fields_15y <- pelotas_2004_raw %>% select(dcmadep, dcotdep, dcundif, icmadep, icotdep, icundif)
dawba_fields_11y <- pelotas_2004_extra_raw %>% select(gdcmadep, gdcotdep, gdcundif, gicmadep, gicotdep, gicundif)
stopifnot(
  all(vapply(dawba_fields_15y, function(x) all(x[!is.na(x)] %in% c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4)), logical(1))),
  all(vapply(dawba_fields_11y, function(x) all(x[!is.na(x)] %in% c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4)), logical(1)))
)

status_data <- pelotas_2004_raw %>%
  select(all_of(core_vars)) %>%
  left_join(puberty_status, by = "idalt20241223", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  left_join(mania_status, by = "idalt20241223", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(
    missing_15y_data = if_any(all_of(predictor_15y_vars), is.na),
    baseline_depression = ifelse(
      !missing_15y_data,
      as.integer(dcmadep != 0 | dcotdep != 0 | dcundif != 0 | icmadep != 0 | icotdep != 0 | icundif != 0),
      NA_integer_
    ),
    missing_18y_outcome = is.na(jsmba6),
    eligibility_status = case_when(
      missing_15y_data                      ~ "Excluded: missing 15y predictor/baseline-diagnosis data",
      !(puberty_data_present %in% TRUE)     ~ "Excluded: missing puberty data",
      is.na(puberty_started)                ~ "Excluded: ambiguous puberty status",
      !(puberty_started %in% TRUE)          ~ "Excluded: pre-pubertal at 15y",
      baseline_depression == 1              ~ "Excluded: baseline (15y) depression",
      missing_18y_outcome                   ~ "Excluded: missing 18y depression outcome (additional loss to follow-up)",
      !(mania_data_present %in% TRUE)       ~ "Excluded: missing mania/hypomania screening data",
      TRUE                                   ~ "Included: valid case"
    ),
    eligibility_group = case_when(
      eligibility_status == "Included: valid case" ~ "Included (final validation sample)",
      eligibility_status %in% c("Excluded: missing 15y predictor/baseline-diagnosis data",
                                 "Excluded: missing puberty data",
                                 "Excluded: ambiguous puberty status",
                                 "Excluded: missing 18y depression outcome (additional loss to follow-up)",
                                 "Excluded: missing mania/hypomania screening data") ~ "Excluded (missing data / attrition)",
      TRUE ~ "Excluded (by design / eligibility criterion)"
    )
  )
stopifnot(nrow(status_data) == n_raw)

## Attach the supplementary variables (used for Tables S5-S6, the IPW model and
## Sensitivities 2-4).
status_data <- status_data %>%
  left_join(
    pelotas_2004_extra_raw %>%
      select(idalt20241223, aescmae4cat, arendsm, fqiwiscstd,
             p1somatic_11, p1worries_11, p1unhappy_11, p1clingy_11, p1afraid_11,
             p1somatic_15, p1worries_15, p1unhappy_15, p1clingy_15, p1afraid_15,
             gdcmadep, gdcotdep, gdcundif, gicmadep, gicotdep, gicundif),
    by = "idalt20241223", relationship = "one-to-one"
  )
stopifnot(nrow(status_data) == n_raw)

## ---- 5. Sequential counts for the flow table ---------------------------------

n_total                 <- nrow(status_data)
n_after_15y             <- sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data)
n_after_puberty_data    <- sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data &
                                  status_data$puberty_data_present %in% TRUE)
n_after_puberty_unambig <- sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data &
                                  status_data$puberty_data_present %in% TRUE &
                                  !is.na(status_data$puberty_started))
n_after_puberty         <- sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data &
                                  status_data$puberty_started %in% TRUE)
n_after_dep             <- sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data &
                                  status_data$puberty_started %in% TRUE &
                                  status_data$baseline_depression == 0)
n_15y_eligible          <- n_after_dep
n_18y_outcome_available <- sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data & status_data$baseline_depression == 0 &
                                  status_data$puberty_started %in% TRUE &
                                  !status_data$missing_18y_outcome)
n_additional_18y_loss    <- n_15y_eligible - n_18y_outcome_available
n_mania_data_available   <- sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data & status_data$baseline_depression == 0 &
                                  status_data$puberty_started %in% TRUE &
                                  !status_data$missing_18y_outcome &
                                  status_data$mania_data_present %in% TRUE)
n_final                  <- n_mania_data_available
n_mania_recoded_nonMDD   <- sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data & status_data$baseline_depression == 0 &
                                  status_data$puberty_started %in% TRUE &
                                  !status_data$missing_18y_outcome &
                                  status_data$mania_data_present %in% TRUE &
                                  status_data$ever_manic_hypomanic %in% TRUE)

flow_table <- tibble(
  Step = c(
    "Enrolled at birth",
    "Complete 15-year data: sex, ethnicity, predictors, baseline diagnosis",
    "Puberty (Tanner staging) data available",
    "Excluding ambiguous puberty status (partial Tanner data)",
    "Excluding pre-pubertal at 15y",
    "Excluding baseline (15y) depression  ->  15-year-eligible sample",
    "Excluding additional loss to follow-up: missing 18-year depression outcome",
    "Excluding missing mania/hypomania screening data  ->  Final validation sample"
  ),
  n_remaining = c(n_total, n_after_15y, n_after_puberty_data,
                   n_after_puberty_unambig, n_after_puberty, n_15y_eligible,
                   n_18y_outcome_available, n_final),
  n_excluded_this_step = c(
    NA,
    n_total - n_after_15y,
    n_after_15y - n_after_puberty_data,
    n_after_puberty_data - n_after_puberty_unambig,
    n_after_puberty_unambig - n_after_puberty,
    n_after_puberty - n_15y_eligible,
    n_additional_18y_loss,
    n_18y_outcome_available - n_final
  )
)
print(flow_table)

## ---- 6. Baseline-depression exclusion: 1993 vs. 2004 ------------------------
## 1993 counts are taken from the published flowchart (Rocha et al., 2021,
## Figure 1a); the 1993 raw data are not used here.

baseline_depression_exclusion <- tibble(
  Cohort = c("Pelotas 1993 (development)", "Pelotas 2004 (this validation)"),
  Screening_instrument = c(
    "SDQ emotional subscale, OR rule across self- and parent-report at ages 11 and 15 (3 informant-timepoints)",
    "DAWBA, caregiver-report only, single wave (age 15)"
  ),
  N_with_screening_data = c(3365L, as.integer(n_after_puberty)),
  N_excluded_positive_screen = c(904L, as.integer(n_after_puberty - n_after_dep)),
  Pct_excluded = round(c(
    100 * 904 / 3365,
    100 * (n_after_puberty - n_after_dep) / n_after_puberty
  ), 1),
  Source = c("Rocha et al. (2021), Figure 1a", "This analysis (see flow table above)")
)
cat("\n--- Baseline-depression exclusion, 1993 vs. 2004 ---\n")
print(baseline_depression_exclusion)

cat(sprintf(
  "\n*** 15-year-eligible sample: N = %d ***\n*** Of these, additional loss to follow-up at 18y (missing depression outcome): n = %d ***\n*** 18-year outcome available: N = %d ***\n*** Final validation sample: N = %d ***\n*** Of these, lifetime manic/hypomanic episode (18y, standard MINI criteria): n = %d -- recoded as NOT having MDD (outcome = 0), fully retained, NOT excluded ***\n",
  n_15y_eligible, n_additional_18y_loss, n_18y_outcome_available, n_final, n_mania_recoded_nonMDD
))

## ---- 7A. Attrition and missing-data analyses --------------------------------
## A. Missingness of the age-15 predictors vs. the age-18 depression outcome.
## B. Additional loss to follow-up between ages 15 and 18 vs. sex, skin colour
## and the 11 IDEA-RS predictors (age-15-eligible sample).
## C. Retention in the final sample vs. sex, skin colour, maternal education and
## household income (full birth cohort).

## -- Section A --
missingness_outcome_data <- pelotas_2004_raw %>%
  mutate(any_predictor_missing = if_any(all_of(predictor_15y_vars), is.na)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(jsmba6))

chisq_missing_outcome <- chisq.test(table(missingness_outcome_data$any_predictor_missing,
                                            missingness_outcome_data$jsmba6))

## -- Section B --
eligible_15y_data <- status_data %>%
  filter(!missing_15y_data & baseline_depression == 0 & puberty_started %in% TRUE)

chisq_18yloss_sex <- chisq.test(table(eligible_15y_data$asexo, eligible_15y_data$missing_18y_outcome))
chisq_18yloss_eth <- chisq.test(table(
  eligible_15y_data$acorpele[!is.na(eligible_15y_data$acorpele)],
  eligible_15y_data$missing_18y_outcome[!is.na(eligible_15y_data$acorpele)]
))

eligible_15y_data <- eligible_15y_data %>%
  mutate(
    drugs_pos     = as.integer(hconfb10a == 1 | hconfb10b == 1 | hconfb10c == 1 | hconfb10d == 1 | hconfb10f == 1),
    school_pos    = as.integer(hgh98 == 1),
    isolation_pos = as.integer(hgf58 == 0),
    fighting_pos  = as.integer(hcmc38 == 1),
    ranaway_pos   = as.integer(hconfc48 == 1),
    maltreat_sum  = hconff109 + hconff110 + hconff111 + hconff112 + hconff113 + hconff114 + hconff115,
    maltreat_cat  = case_when(maltreat_sum == 0 ~ "None", maltreat_sum == 1 ~ "Probable", maltreat_sum >= 2 ~ "Severe"),
    rel_mother_cat  = ifelse(hconfc51 == 6, 5, as.numeric(hconfc51)),
    rel_father_cat  = ifelse(hconfc49 == 6, 5, as.numeric(hconfc49)),
    rel_between_cat = ifelse(hconfc53 == 6, 5, as.numeric(hconfc53))
  )

attrition_predictor_vars <- list(
  "Drug use"                      = eligible_15y_data$drugs_pos,
  "School failure"                = eligible_15y_data$school_pos,
  "Social isolation"              = eligible_15y_data$isolation_pos,
  "Fight involvement"             = eligible_15y_data$fighting_pos,
  "Ran away from home"            = eligible_15y_data$ranaway_pos,
  "Childhood maltreatment"        = eligible_15y_data$maltreat_cat,
  "Relationship with mother"      = eligible_15y_data$rel_mother_cat,
  "Relationship with father"      = eligible_15y_data$rel_father_cat,
  "Relationship between parents"  = eligible_15y_data$rel_between_cat
)

attrition_predictor_checks <- purrr::imap_dfr(attrition_predictor_vars, function(v, name) {
  tst <- chisq.test(table(v, eligible_15y_data$missing_18y_outcome))
  tibble(Comparison = name, Chi_sq = round(unname(tst$statistic), 3),
         df = unname(tst$parameter), p_value = round(tst$p.value, 3))
})

## -- Section C --
baseline_attrition_data <- status_data %>%
  mutate(
    in_final_sample = eligibility_status == "Included: valid case",
    income_quartile = ntile(arendsm, 4)
  )

chisq_baseline_sex <- chisq.test(table(baseline_attrition_data$asexo, baseline_attrition_data$in_final_sample))
chisq_baseline_eth <- chisq.test(table(
  baseline_attrition_data$acorpele[!is.na(baseline_attrition_data$acorpele)],
  baseline_attrition_data$in_final_sample[!is.na(baseline_attrition_data$acorpele)]
))
## Participants with missing maternal education are left out of this test (not
## imputed), as for skin colour.
chisq_baseline_educ <- chisq.test(table(
  baseline_attrition_data$aescmae4cat[!is.na(baseline_attrition_data$aescmae4cat)],
  baseline_attrition_data$in_final_sample[!is.na(baseline_attrition_data$aescmae4cat)]
))
chisq_baseline_income <- chisq.test(table(
  baseline_attrition_data$income_quartile[!is.na(baseline_attrition_data$income_quartile)],
  baseline_attrition_data$in_final_sample[!is.na(baseline_attrition_data$income_quartile)]
))

attrition_chisq_tests <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    Section = "A. Missingness on the age-15 predictor block vs. the 18-year depression outcome (among participants with an observed 18-year diagnosis)",
    Comparison = "Any predictor missing vs. depression outcome",
    Chi_sq = round(unname(chisq_missing_outcome$statistic), 3),
    df = unname(chisq_missing_outcome$parameter),
    p_value = round(chisq_missing_outcome$p.value, 3)
  ),
  tibble(
    Section = "B. Additional loss to follow-up between the 15- and 18-year waves (among the 15-year-eligible sample)",
    Comparison = "Sex",
    Chi_sq = round(unname(chisq_18yloss_sex$statistic), 3),
    df = unname(chisq_18yloss_sex$parameter),
    p_value = round(chisq_18yloss_sex$p.value, 3)
  ),
  tibble(
    Section = "B. Additional loss to follow-up between the 15- and 18-year waves (among the 15-year-eligible sample)",
    Comparison = "Skin colour",
    Chi_sq = round(unname(chisq_18yloss_eth$statistic), 3),
    df = unname(chisq_18yloss_eth$parameter),
    p_value = round(chisq_18yloss_eth$p.value, 3)
  ),
  attrition_predictor_checks %>% mutate(Section = "B. Additional loss to follow-up between the 15- and 18-year waves (among the 15-year-eligible sample)", .before = 1),
  tibble(
    Section = "C. Retention in the final analytic sample vs. exclusion at any step (full birth cohort, N=4,231)",
    Comparison = "Sex",
    Chi_sq = round(unname(chisq_baseline_sex$statistic), 3),
    df = unname(chisq_baseline_sex$parameter),
    p_value = round(chisq_baseline_sex$p.value, 3)
  ),
  tibble(
    Section = "C. Retention in the final analytic sample vs. exclusion at any step (full birth cohort, N=4,231)",
    Comparison = "Skin colour",
    Chi_sq = round(unname(chisq_baseline_eth$statistic), 3),
    df = unname(chisq_baseline_eth$parameter),
    p_value = round(chisq_baseline_eth$p.value, 3)
  ),
  tibble(
    Section = "C. Retention in the final analytic sample vs. exclusion at any step (full birth cohort, N=4,231)",
    Comparison = "Maternal education (4 categories)",
    Chi_sq = round(unname(chisq_baseline_educ$statistic), 3),
    df = unname(chisq_baseline_educ$parameter),
    p_value = round(chisq_baseline_educ$p.value, 3)
  ),
  tibble(
    Section = "C. Retention in the final analytic sample vs. exclusion at any step (full birth cohort, N=4,231)",
    Comparison = "Household income (quartiles)",
    Chi_sq = round(unname(chisq_baseline_income$statistic), 3),
    df = unname(chisq_baseline_income$parameter),
    p_value = round(chisq_baseline_income$p.value, 3)
  )
)
cat("\n--- Attrition chi-sq tests (diagnostic, not in manuscript) ---\n")
print(attrition_chisq_tests, n = Inf)

## ---- 7B. Eligibility and missingness tables (Tables S3 and S4) --------------
## Table S3: every exclusion reason in the cascade, tagged as an eligibility
## criterion (by design) or as missing data / attrition.
eligibility_summary <- status_data %>%
  count(eligibility_group, eligibility_status, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(pct_of_birth_cohort = round(100 * n / n_total, 1)) %>%
  arrange(eligibility_group) %>%
  rename(`Eligibility group` = eligibility_group, Status = eligibility_status,
         N = n, `% of birth cohort` = pct_of_birth_cohort)
cat("\n--- Table S3: eligibility (intentional exclusion) vs. attrition (non-observation), full cascade ---\n")
print(eligibility_summary, n = Inf)

## Table S4: missingness of each age-15 predictor, puberty status and the
## baseline-depression screen, and its association with the age-18 outcome. One
## row per derived predictor or questionnaire module; the six DAWBA fields,
## seven maltreatment items and five drug-use items are each collapsed into one
## row. A module is coded missing if any of its items is missing. Puberty status
## is reported alongside the DAWBA screen because both are exclusion criteria
## rather than predictors.
predictor_groups_ordered <- c(
  "Sex", "Skin colour",
  "Baseline depression screen (DAWBA) — exclusion criterion, not an IDEA-RS predictor",
  "Childhood maltreatment", "Any drug use", "School failure", "Social isolation",
  "Fight involvement", "Ran away from home", "Relationship with father",
  "Relationship with mother", "Relationship between parents"
)
stopifnot(setequal(predictor_groups_ordered, unique(predictor_15y_var_groups)))

## Fixed-decimal formatting, so every row shows the same number of decimals.
## p-values are floored at "<0.001"; "—" is shown where no test is possible.
format_stat <- function(x, digits = 3) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
format_p_em <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", ifelse(x < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", x)))

## Shared by the predictor loop and the puberty row. N_total is the same for
## every row (participants with an observed age-18 outcome).
run_missingness_test <- function(is_missing, outcome) {
  d <- tibble(missing = is_missing, outcome = outcome) %>% filter(!is.na(outcome))
  n_total <- nrow(d)
  n_miss  <- sum(d$missing)
  ## With 0% or 100% missingness there is nothing to test (chisq.test() on a
  ## one-row table would run a goodness-of-fit test), so that case is excluded
  ## explicitly.
  tst <- if (n_miss > 0 && n_miss < n_total) {
    tryCatch(chisq.test(table(d$missing, d$outcome)), error = function(e) NULL)
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  tibble(
    N_total = n_total,
    N_missing = n_miss,
    Pct_missing = round(100 * n_miss / n_total, 1),
    Chi_sq = if (!is.null(tst)) format_stat(unname(tst$statistic)) else "—",
    df = if (!is.null(tst)) as.character(unname(tst$parameter)) else "—",
    p_value = if (!is.null(tst)) format_p_em(tst$p.value) else "—"
  )
}

predictor_missingness_by_var <- purrr::map_dfr(predictor_groups_ordered, function(g) {
  vars_in_group <- names(predictor_15y_var_groups)[predictor_15y_var_groups == g]
  na_mat <- is.na(as.data.frame(pelotas_2004_raw)[, vars_in_group, drop = FALSE])
  is_missing <- if (ncol(na_mat) == 1) na_mat[, 1] else apply(na_mat, 1, any)
  bind_cols(
    tibble(Variable = if (length(vars_in_group) > 1) sprintf("%s (%d items)", g, length(vars_in_group)) else g),
    run_missingness_test(is_missing, pelotas_2004_raw$jsmba6)
  )
})

## Puberty status (Tanner stage) is derived from sex-specific fields
## (hconfmasce87/88 for boys, hconffeme87/88 for girls; see Section 3), so it is
## computed separately from the generic loop.
puberty_missing_vec <- with(pelotas_2004_raw, ifelse(
  asexo == 1, is.na(hconfmasce87) & is.na(hconfmasce88),
  ifelse(asexo == 2, is.na(hconffeme87) & is.na(hconffeme88), NA)
))
stopifnot(!anyNA(puberty_missing_vec))  # asexo is 1 or 2 for every participant
puberty_row <- bind_cols(
  tibble(Variable = "Puberty status (Tanner stage) — exclusion criterion, not an IDEA-RS predictor"),
  run_missingness_test(puberty_missing_vec, pelotas_2004_raw$jsmba6)
)

## Puberty row inserted after Skin colour and before the DAWBA row, following
## the order of the exclusion criteria in the Methods.
predictor_missingness_by_var <- bind_rows(
  predictor_missingness_by_var[1:2, ],
  puberty_row,
  predictor_missingness_by_var[3:nrow(predictor_missingness_by_var), ]
)

stopifnot(length(unique(predictor_missingness_by_var$N_total)) == 1)  # denominator must be constant across rows
table_s4_total_n <- predictor_missingness_by_var$N_total[1]
predictor_missingness_by_var <- predictor_missingness_by_var %>%
  select(-N_total) %>%
  rename(`N missing` = N_missing, `% missing` = Pct_missing, `χ²` = Chi_sq, `p value` = p_value)

cat(sprintf("\n--- Table S4: missingness by predictor (age-15 block, grouped by questionnaire module) vs. 18-year outcome (N=%d) ---\n", table_s4_total_n))
print(predictor_missingness_by_var, n = Inf, width = Inf)

## ---- 8. Final analytic dataset (main analysis) ------------------------------
## All participants with mania screening data (N = n_final). A lifetime
## manic/hypomanic episode does not remove anyone: depression_outcome is set to
## 0.

## Applies the predictor recoding and outcome definition to any set of subject
## IDs, so the main analysis and every sensitivity sample share one
## implementation.
build_analytic_dataset <- function(ids) {
  d <- status_data %>% filter(idalt20241223 %in% ids)

  ## Each maltreatment item must be 0/1 (summed into none / probable / severe);
  ## a miscoded value fails loudly.
  maltreat_items <- d %>% select(hconff109, hconff110, hconff111, hconff112, hconff113, hconff114, hconff115)
  stopifnot(all(vapply(maltreat_items, function(x) all(x %in% c(0, 1)), logical(1))))

  d %>%
    mutate(
      maltreatment_sum = hconff109 + hconff110 + hconff111 + hconff112 + hconff113 + hconff114 + hconff115,
      maltreatment = case_when(
        maltreatment_sum == 0 ~ 0,
        maltreatment_sum == 1 ~ 1,
        maltreatment_sum >= 2 ~ 2
      ),
      drugs = ifelse(hconfb10a == 1 | hconfb10b == 1 | hconfb10c == 1 | hconfb10d == 1 | hconfb10f == 1, 1, 0),
      sex = ifelse(asexo == 2, 1, 0),
      ## Skin colour: acorpele, caregiver-reported at the age-6 wave (4
      ## categories; 1 = white), the only skin-colour variable in the 2004 data
      ## files.
      ethnicity = ifelse(acorpele == 1, 0, 1),
      ## Social isolation: hgf58 == 0, as in the 1993 item (Rocha et al., 2021,
      ## Table S1).
      social_isolation = ifelse(hgf58 == 0, 1, 0),
      ## School failure, fighting and running away are coded 1 = yes on their
      ## raw scales and are dichotomised here before entering the linear
      ## predictor.
      school_failure = as.integer(hgh98 == 1),
      fighting = as.integer(hcmc38 == 1),
      ran_away = as.integer(hconfc48 == 1),

      ## Raw relationship categories (1-6), kept for Table 1.
      rel_mother_raw  = as.numeric(hconfc51),
      rel_father_raw  = as.numeric(hconfc49),
      rel_between_raw = as.numeric(hconfc53),

      ## Main analysis: "no father / mother / parental figure present" (code 6)
      ## is recoded to "bad" (5).
      father_recoded_to_ref  = hconfc49 == 6,
      mother_recoded_to_ref  = hconfc51 == 6,
      between_recoded_to_ref = hconfc53 == 6,
      rel_mother_cat  = ifelse(hconfc51 == 6, 5, as.numeric(hconfc51)),
      rel_father_cat  = ifelse(hconfc49 == 6, 5, as.numeric(hconfc49)),
      rel_between_cat = ifelse(hconfc53 == 6, 5, as.numeric(hconfc53)),

      ## Lifetime manic/hypomanic episode (standard MINI criteria): recoded as a
      ## non-case (0) and retained.
      depression_outcome = ifelse(ever_manic_hypomanic %in% TRUE, 0, as.numeric(jsmba6))
    ) %>%
    select(
      subject_id = idalt20241223,
      sex, ethnicity, drugs, maltreatment,
      school_failure, social_isolation, fighting, ran_away,
      rel_mother_cat, rel_father_cat, rel_between_cat,
      rel_mother_raw, rel_father_raw, rel_between_raw,
      father_recoded_to_ref, mother_recoded_to_ref, between_recoded_to_ref,
      ever_manic_hypomanic,
      depression_outcome
    )
}

main_ids <- status_data %>% filter(eligibility_status == "Included: valid case") %>% pull(idalt20241223)
pel_2004_desc <- build_analytic_dataset(main_ids)

stopifnot(n_analytic == n_final, nrow(pel_2004_desc) == length(main_ids))

## ---- 9. Table 1: predictor distributions ------------------------------------
## 1993 counts are the published counts from Rocha et al. (2021), Table 1 (J Am
## Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry 60(2):262-273).

n_1993 <- 2192
n_2004 <- nrow(pel_2004_valid)

test_binary_exact <- function(n1993_pos, n2004_pos, n2004_total) {
  tab <- matrix(c(n1993_pos, n_1993 - n1993_pos,
                  n2004_pos, n2004_total - n2004_pos), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  tryCatch(chisq.test(tab)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

test_grouped_exact <- function(n1993_vec, n2004_vec) {
  tab <- rbind(n1993_vec, n2004_vec)
  tryCatch(chisq.test(tab)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

format_p <- function(p) {
  case_when(
    is.na(p)   ~ "-",
    p < 0.001  ~ "<0.001",
    TRUE       ~ sprintf("%.3f", p)
  )
}

fmt_n_pct <- function(n, pct) {
  ifelse(is.na(n), "-", sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", as.integer(n), pct))
}

binary_defs <- tribble(
  ~Predictor,                        ~n_1993_exact, ~var_2004,           ~positive_value,
  "Female sex",                       1215,          "sex",                1,
  "Non-white skin color",              714,          "ethnicity",          1,
  "School failure (grade retention)", 1127,          "school_failure",     1,
  "Social isolation",                  231,          "social_isolation",   1,
  "Fight involvement",                 211,          "fighting",           1,
  "Ran away from home",                 80,          "ran_away",           1,
  "Any drug use",                     1367,          "drugs",              1
)

    Pelotas_2004_pct = round(100 * n2004_pos / n_2004, 1),
    Pelotas_1993_pct = round(100 * n_1993_exact / n_1993, 1),
    p_value = test_binary_exact(n_1993_exact, n2004_pos, n_2004)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(
    Group = Predictor, Category = NA_character_,
    Pelotas_1993_n = n_1993_exact, Pelotas_1993_pct,
    Pelotas_2004_n = n2004_pos, Pelotas_2004_pct,
    p_value_fmt = format_p(p_value)
  )

  Pelotas_2004_n = as.integer(malt_2004_n), Pelotas_2004_pct = round(100 * malt_2004_n / n_2004, 1),
  p_value_fmt = c(format_p(malt_p), "", "")

build_rel_group_full <- function(group_label, var_2004_raw, n1993_vec5, label_6) {
  cats <- c(Great = 1, `Very good` = 2, Good = 3, Regular = 4, Bad = 5)
  n2004_vec5 <- sapply(cats, function(v) sum(pel_2004_valid[[var_2004_raw]] == v, na.rm = TRUE))
  n2004_cat6 <- sum(pel_2004_valid[[var_2004_raw]] == 6, na.rm = TRUE)
  n2004_vec6 <- c(n2004_vec5, n2004_cat6)
  ## The chi-square test compares the five-category distribution, with the 2004
  ## sixth category ("no figure present") folded into "Bad" as in build_lp().
  ## 1993 has no sixth category, so including it would test against a structural
  ## zero.
  n2004_vec5_recoded <- n2004_vec5
  n2004_vec5_recoded["Bad"] <- n2004_vec5_recoded["Bad"] + n2004_cat6
  p <- test_grouped_exact(n1993_vec5, n2004_vec5_recoded)
  tibble(
    Group = group_label,
    Category = c(names(cats), label_6),
    Pelotas_1993_n = c(n1993_vec5, NA), Pelotas_1993_pct = c(round(100 * n1993_vec5 / n_1993, 1), NA),
    Pelotas_2004_n = as.integer(n2004_vec6), Pelotas_2004_pct = round(100 * n2004_vec6 / n_2004, 1),
    p_value_fmt = c(format_p(p), rep("", 5))
  )
}

## ---- 11. Reusable linear-predictor builder -----------------------------------

build_lp <- function(data) {
  data %>%
    mutate(
      mom_2 = as.integer(rel_mother_cat == 2), mom_3 = as.integer(rel_mother_cat == 3),
      mom_4 = as.integer(rel_mother_cat == 4), mom_5 = as.integer(rel_mother_cat == 5),
      dad_2 = as.integer(rel_father_cat == 2), dad_3 = as.integer(rel_father_cat == 3),
      dad_4 = as.integer(rel_father_cat == 4), dad_5 = as.integer(rel_father_cat == 5),
      btw_2 = as.integer(rel_between_cat == 2), btw_3 = as.integer(rel_between_cat == 3),
      btw_4 = as.integer(rel_between_cat == 4), btw_5 = as.integer(rel_between_cat == 5),
      maltreatment_prob   = ifelse(maltreatment == 1, 1, 0),
      maltreatment_severe = ifelse(maltreatment == 2, 1, 0),
      across(c(sex, ethnicity, school_failure, drugs, social_isolation, fighting, ran_away, depression_outcome), as.numeric)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      lp = coef_pmle$intercept +
        coef_pmle$sex * sex + coef_pmle$ethnicity * ethnicity + coef_pmle$school_failure * school_failure +
        coef_pmle$drugs * drugs + coef_pmle$social_isolation * social_isolation + coef_pmle$fighting * fighting +
        coef_pmle$ran_away * ran_away +
        coef_pmle$maltreatment_prob * maltreatment_prob + coef_pmle$maltreatment_severe * maltreatment_severe +
        coef_pmle$mom_2*mom_2 + coef_pmle$mom_3*mom_3 + coef_pmle$mom_4*mom_4 + coef_pmle$mom_5*mom_5 +
        coef_pmle$dad_2*dad_2 + coef_pmle$dad_3*dad_3 + coef_pmle$dad_4*dad_4 + coef_pmle$dad_5*dad_5 +
        coef_pmle$btw_2*btw_2 + coef_pmle$btw_3*btw_3 + coef_pmle$btw_4*btw_4 + coef_pmle$btw_5*btw_5 +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_ethnicity*sex*ethnicity + coef_pmle$sex_x_school_fail*sex*school_failure +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_drugs*sex*drugs + coef_pmle$sex_x_social_iso*sex*social_isolation +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_fighting*sex*fighting + coef_pmle$sex_x_ran_away*sex*ran_away +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_prob_malt*sex*maltreatment_prob + coef_pmle$sex_x_severe_malt*sex*maltreatment_severe +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_mom_2*sex*mom_2 + coef_pmle$sex_x_mom_3*sex*mom_3 +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_mom_4*sex*mom_4 + coef_pmle$sex_x_mom_5*sex*mom_5 +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_dad_2*sex*dad_2 + coef_pmle$sex_x_dad_3*sex*dad_3 +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_dad_4*sex*dad_4 + coef_pmle$sex_x_dad_5*sex*dad_5 +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_btw_2*sex*btw_2 + coef_pmle$sex_x_btw_3*sex*btw_3 +
        coef_pmle$sex_x_btw_4*sex*btw_4 + coef_pmle$sex_x_btw_5*sex*btw_5,
      predicted_prob = 1 / (1 + exp(-lp))
    )
}

pel_2004_model <- build_lp(pel_2004_valid)

## ---- 12. Validation metrics and bootstrap -----------------------------------
## compute_validation_metrics(): point estimates with analytic CIs for the
## C-statistic (DeLong), calibration intercept and slope (Wald) and O/E ratio
## (exact Poisson). All tables report bootstrap CIs (bootstrap_all_metrics), so
## one method is used for every metric.

compute_validation_metrics <- function(y, p, lp) {
  ## Direction is fixed explicitly: with "auto", a resample in which the case
  ## and control medians invert would silently flip the AUC above 0.5.
  roc_obj <- pROC::roc(response = y, predictor = p, levels = c(0, 1), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
  c_stat  <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_obj))
  c_ci    <- as.numeric(pROC::ci.auc(roc_obj, method = "delong"))

  mean_p <- mean(p); mean_y <- mean(y)
  mean_cal_error <- mean_p - mean_y

  citl_model   <- glm(y ~ offset(lp), family = binomial)
  citl_logodds <- unname(coef(citl_model)[1])

  cal_model <- glm(y ~ lp, family = binomial)
  cal_ci <- confint.default(cal_model)
  cal_intercept <- unname(coef(cal_model)[1]); cal_slope <- unname(coef(cal_model)[2])

  brier <- mean((y - p)^2)
  loess_pred <- predict(loess(y ~ p, span = 0.75, degree = 1), p)
  abs_cal_error <- abs(loess_pred - p)
  ici  <- mean(abs_cal_error, na.rm = TRUE)
  e50  <- median(abs_cal_error, na.rm = TRUE)
  e90  <- as.numeric(quantile(abs_cal_error, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE))
  emax <- max(abs_cal_error, na.rm = TRUE)

  O <- as.integer(round(sum(y))); E <- sum(p)
  oe_test <- poisson.test(x = O, T = E)

  ## Full precision is returned; rounding happens only at display time (fmt_est,
  ## fmt_ci_boot), so bootstrap quantiles are not taken over rounded values.
  list(
    metrics = tibble(
      n = length(y), n_events = O, expected_events = E,
      c_statistic = c_stat, c_lower = c_ci[1], c_upper = c_ci[3],
      mean_cal_error = mean_cal_error,
      citl_logodds = citl_logodds,
      cal_intercept = cal_intercept, cal_intercept_lower = cal_ci[1,1], cal_intercept_upper = cal_ci[1,2],
      cal_slope = cal_slope, cal_slope_lower = cal_ci[2,1], cal_slope_upper = cal_ci[2,2],
      brier = brier,
      ici = ici, e50 = e50, e90 = e90, emax = emax,
      OE_ratio = O / E, OE_lower = oe_test$conf.int[1], OE_upper = oe_test$conf.int[2]
    ),
    roc = roc_obj
  )
}

## Weighted empirical quantile (linear interpolation of the weighted CDF);
## stats::quantile() has no weights argument.
weighted_quantile <- function(x, w, probs) {
  ord <- order(x)
  x <- x[ord]; w <- w[ord]
  cum_w <- cumsum(w) / sum(w)
  as.numeric(approx(cum_w, x, xout = probs, rule = 2)$y)
}

## Weighted counterpart of compute_validation_metrics(), used for the IPW
## sensitivity analysis. Each statistic is a closed-form weighted quantity (no
## resampling), so it can be used for the point estimate and inside a bootstrap
## replicate. pROC has no weighted AUC (WeightedROC is used instead);
## quasibinomial is used for the calibration models to avoid warnings about
## non-integer successes under continuous weights (point estimates are identical
## to binomial).
compute_weighted_validation_metrics <- function(y, p, lp, w) {
  wroc   <- WeightedROC::WeightedROC(p, y, w)
  c_stat <- WeightedROC::WeightedAUC(wroc)

  mean_p <- weighted.mean(p, w); mean_y <- weighted.mean(y, w)
  mean_cal_error <- mean_p - mean_y

  citl_model_w <- glm(y ~ offset(lp), family = quasibinomial, weights = w)
  citl_logodds <- unname(coef(citl_model_w)[1])

  cal_model_w <- glm(y ~ lp, family = quasibinomial, weights = w)
  cal_intercept <- unname(coef(cal_model_w)[1]); cal_slope <- unname(coef(cal_model_w)[2])

  brier <- weighted.mean((y - p)^2, w)

  loess_fit_w <- loess(y ~ p, weights = w, span = 0.75, degree = 1)
  loess_pred_w <- predict(loess_fit_w, p)
  abs_cal_error_w <- abs(loess_pred_w - p)
  ici  <- weighted.mean(abs_cal_error_w, w, na.rm = TRUE)
  e50  <- weighted_quantile(abs_cal_error_w, w, 0.50)
  e90  <- weighted_quantile(abs_cal_error_w, w, 0.90)
  emax <- max(abs_cal_error_w, na.rm = TRUE)

  ## Weighted O/E ratio: weighted observed over weighted expected events.
  O <- sum(w * y); E <- sum(w * p)

  ## Full precision returned, as in compute_validation_metrics().
  tibble(
    n = length(y), n_events = sum(y), expected_events = E,
    c_statistic = c_stat,
    mean_cal_error = mean_cal_error,
    citl_logodds = citl_logodds,
    cal_intercept = cal_intercept,
    cal_slope = cal_slope,
    brier = brier,
    ici = ici, e50 = e50, e90 = e90, emax = emax,
    OE_ratio = O / E
  )
}

## Metrics that are bootstrapped (point-estimate columns only, not the analytic
## CI columns).
BOOTSTRAP_METRIC_NAMES <- c("c_statistic", "mean_cal_error", "citl_logodds", "cal_intercept",
                             "cal_slope", "OE_ratio", "brier", "ici", "e50", "e90", "emax")

## Runs one bootstrap replicate: warnings are counted in warn_env$n (not
## printed) and the replicate is dropped (NULL) on error. warning: false in the
## YAML header hides warning text, so these counts keep the warning rate
## visible.
run_boot_replicate <- function(expr, warn_env) {
  tryCatch(
    withCallingHandlers(
      expr,
      warning = function(w) {
        assign("n", warn_env$n + 1, envir = warn_env)
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
}

## Generic bootstrap engine. Resamples rows with replacement and recomputes
## compute_validation_metrics() on each resample. The point estimate is the
## metric on the original data; CIs are the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles across
## replicates.
bootstrap_all_metrics <- function(data, prob_col, lp_col, outcome_col = "depression_outcome",
                                    n_boot = N_BOOT, seed = 2024) {
  set.seed(seed)
  n <- nrow(data)
  probs <- rep(1 / n, n)

  ## Degenerate resamples (e.g. a loess fit that does not converge) are dropped
  ## rather than aborting the run; failures are counted and reported.
  boot_list <- vector("list", n_boot)
  warn_env <- new.env(); warn_env$n <- 0
  for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    idx <- sample.int(n, size = n, replace = TRUE, prob = probs)
    rs  <- data[idx, ]
    boot_list[[b]] <- run_boot_replicate(
      compute_validation_metrics(rs[[outcome_col]], rs[[prob_col]], rs[[lp_col]])$metrics,
      warn_env
    )
  }
  n_failed <- sum(vapply(boot_list, is.null, logical(1)))
  if (n_failed > 0) cat(sprintf("  (bootstrap: %d/%d replicates failed and were dropped)\n", n_failed, n_boot))
  if (warn_env$n > 0) cat(sprintf("  (bootstrap: %d warnings raised across %d replicates)\n", warn_env$n, n_boot))
  boot_df <- bind_rows(boot_list)

  point <- compute_validation_metrics(data[[outcome_col]], data[[prob_col]], data[[lp_col]])$metrics

  out <- point
  for (m in BOOTSTRAP_METRIC_NAMES) {
    out[[paste0(m, "_lo")]] <- round(as.numeric(quantile(boot_df[[m]], 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)), 4)
    out[[paste0(m, "_hi")]] <- round(as.numeric(quantile(boot_df[[m]], 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)), 4)
  }
  out
}

## Two-column (original vs. recalibrated) table formatter with bootstrap CIs;
## used for Table 2 and each sensitivity analysis.
fmt_est <- function(x, digits = 2) sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), round(x, digits))
fmt_ci_boot <- function(est, lo, hi, digits = 2) {
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"),
          round(est, digits), round(lo, digits), round(hi, digits))
}

build_table2_style <- function(boot_std, boot_recal) {
  tibble(
    `Performance parameter` = c(
      "C-statistic (95% CI)",
      "Mean calibration error (predicted - observed)",
      "Calibration-in-the-large (log-odds scale)",
      "Calibration intercept (95% CI)",
      "Calibration slope (95% CI)",
      "O/E ratio (95% CI)",
      "Brier score",
      "ICI / E-avg (mean absolute calibration error)",
      "E50 (median absolute calibration error)",
      "E90 (90th percentile absolute calibration error)",
      "Emax (max. absolute calibration error)"
    ),
    `Original model` = c(
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$c_statistic, boot_std$c_statistic_lo, boot_std$c_statistic_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$mean_cal_error, boot_std$mean_cal_error_lo, boot_std$mean_cal_error_hi, 3),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$citl_logodds, boot_std$citl_logodds_lo, boot_std$citl_logodds_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$cal_intercept, boot_std$cal_intercept_lo, boot_std$cal_intercept_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$cal_slope, boot_std$cal_slope_lo, boot_std$cal_slope_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$OE_ratio, boot_std$OE_ratio_lo, boot_std$OE_ratio_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$brier, boot_std$brier_lo, boot_std$brier_hi, 3),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$ici, boot_std$ici_lo, boot_std$ici_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$e50, boot_std$e50_lo, boot_std$e50_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$e90, boot_std$e90_lo, boot_std$e90_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_std$emax, boot_std$emax_lo, boot_std$emax_hi)
    ),
    `Recalibrated model` = c(
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$c_statistic, boot_recal$c_statistic_lo, boot_recal$c_statistic_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$mean_cal_error, boot_recal$mean_cal_error_lo, boot_recal$mean_cal_error_hi, 3),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$citl_logodds, boot_recal$citl_logodds_lo, boot_recal$citl_logodds_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$cal_intercept, boot_recal$cal_intercept_lo, boot_recal$cal_intercept_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$cal_slope, boot_recal$cal_slope_lo, boot_recal$cal_slope_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$OE_ratio, boot_recal$OE_ratio_lo, boot_recal$OE_ratio_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$brier, boot_recal$brier_lo, boot_recal$brier_hi, 3),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$ici, boot_recal$ici_lo, boot_recal$ici_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$e50, boot_recal$e50_lo, boot_recal$e50_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$e90, boot_recal$e90_lo, boot_recal$e90_hi),
      fmt_ci_boot(boot_recal$emax, boot_recal$emax_lo, boot_recal$emax_hi)
    )
  )
}

## Prevalence-gap decomposition: the rise from the 1993 prevalence (3.1%) to the
## observed prevalence, split into the part explained by case-mix (mean
## predicted risk) and an unexplained residual. Optional weights are used for
## the IPW sensitivity analysis.
decompose_prevalence_gap <- function(outcome, predicted_prob, weights = NULL, dev_prevalence = 3.1) {
  if (is.null(weights)) {
    obs_prev  <- 100 * mean(outcome)
    mean_pred <- 100 * mean(predicted_prob)
  } else {
    obs_prev  <- 100 * weighted.mean(outcome, weights)
    mean_pred <- 100 * weighted.mean(predicted_prob, weights)
  }
  tibble(
    Observed_prevalence_pct   = round(obs_prev, 1),
    Mean_predicted_risk_pct   = round(mean_pred, 2),
    Dev_cohort_prevalence_pct = dev_prevalence,
    Total_gap_pct             = round(obs_prev - dev_prevalence, 1),
    Casemix_explained_pct     = round(mean_pred - dev_prevalence, 1),
    Residual_pct              = round(obs_prev - mean_pred, 1)
  )
}

## Calibration plot (loess curve and decile points with Wilson intervals),
## unweighted or weighted; used for Figure 3 and the sensitivity plots.
build_calibration_plot <- function(data, prob_col, outcome_col, weight_col = NULL, title) {
  if (is.null(weight_col)) {
    loess_fit <- loess(as.formula(paste(outcome_col, "~", prob_col)), data = data, span = 0.75, degree = 1)
  } else {
    loess_fit <- loess(as.formula(paste(outcome_col, "~", prob_col)), data = data, span = 0.75, degree = 1,
                        weights = data[[weight_col]])
  }

  trim_range <- quantile(data[[prob_col]], c(0.01, 0.99))
  pred_range <- seq(trim_range[1], trim_range[2], length.out = 200)
  loess_pred <- predict(loess_fit, newdata = setNames(data.frame(pred_range), prob_col), se = TRUE)

  loess_df <- tibble(
    x = pred_range, fit = loess_pred$fit,
    lower = loess_pred$fit - 1.96 * loess_pred$se.fit,
    upper = loess_pred$fit + 1.96 * loess_pred$se.fit
  )

  data <- data %>% mutate(.decile = ntile(.data[[prob_col]], 10))

  if (is.null(weight_col)) {
    binned <- data %>% group_by(.decile) %>%
      summarise(mean_predicted = mean(.data[[prob_col]]), mean_observed = mean(.data[[outcome_col]]), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  } else {
    binned <- data %>% group_by(.decile) %>%
      summarise(mean_predicted = weighted.mean(.data[[prob_col]], .data[[weight_col]]),
                mean_observed  = weighted.mean(.data[[outcome_col]], .data[[weight_col]]),
                n = n(), .groups = "drop")
  }

  ## Wilson score intervals: several deciles have low event proportions, where
  ## Wald intervals can extend below 0.
  z <- 1.96
  binned <- binned %>%
    mutate(
      wilson_center    = (mean_observed + z^2 / (2 * n)) / (1 + z^2 / n),
      wilson_halfwidth = z * sqrt(mean_observed * (1 - mean_observed) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / (1 + z^2 / n),
      ci_lower = pmax(wilson_center - wilson_halfwidth, 0),
      ci_upper = pmin(wilson_center + wilson_halfwidth, 1)
    )

  ggplot() +
    geom_ribbon(data = loess_df, aes(x = x, ymin = pmax(lower, 0), ymax = pmin(upper, 1)),
                fill = PLOT_BLUE, alpha = 0.15) +
    geom_line(data = loess_df, aes(x = x, y = fit), color = PLOT_BLUE, linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = binned, aes(mean_predicted, mean_observed), size = 3) +
    geom_errorbar(data = binned,
                   aes(x = mean_predicted, ymin = ci_lower, ymax = ci_upper),
                   width = 0.01) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
    coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 0.5), ylim = c(0, 0.5)) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Predicted probability", y = "Observed frequency") +
    theme_bw()
}

## ---- 13. Main analysis: standard + recalibrated validation (Table 2) --------

result_standard   <- compute_validation_metrics(pel_2004_model$depression_outcome, pel_2004_model$predicted_prob, pel_2004_model$lp)
metrics_standard  <- result_standard$metrics
roc_standard       <- result_standard$roc

## The recalibrated intercept is estimated once on the full sample and then held
## fixed, so bootstrap CIs for the recalibrated metrics reflect sampling
## variability conditional on that intercept.
recal_model   <- glm(depression_outcome ~ offset(lp), data = pel_2004_model, family = binomial)
new_intercept <- coef(recal_model)[1]
cat(sprintf("\nRecalibrated intercept: %.3f (original: %.3f)\n", new_intercept, coef_pmle$intercept))

pel_2004_model <- pel_2004_model %>%
  mutate(lp_recal = lp + new_intercept, predicted_prob_recal = 1 / (1 + exp(-lp_recal)))

result_recal   <- compute_validation_metrics(pel_2004_model$depression_outcome, pel_2004_model$predicted_prob_recal, pel_2004_model$lp_recal)
metrics_recal  <- result_recal$metrics

cat("\n--- Original model ---\n"); print(metrics_standard)
cat("\n--- Recalibrated model ---\n"); print(metrics_recal)

boot_main_std   <- bootstrap_all_metrics(pel_2004_model, "predicted_prob",       "lp",        n_boot = N_BOOT)
boot_main_recal <- bootstrap_all_metrics(pel_2004_model, "predicted_prob_recal", "lp_recal",  n_boot = N_BOOT)

table2_manuscript <- build_table2_style(boot_main_std, boot_main_recal)

## ---- 15. Figure 2 (ROC) and Figure 3 (calibration) --------------------------
## One ROC curve is shown: recalibrating the intercept does not change the
## ranking of predicted risks, so the ROC curve and C-statistic are identical
## for the original and recalibrated models.

get_threshold_points <- function(roc_obj, thresholds, labels) {
  coords_df <- pROC::coords(roc_obj, x = thresholds, input = "threshold",
                             ret = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity"))
  coords_df %>% mutate(label = labels)
}

## Threshold markers are recalibrated risk cut-offs (5%, 10%, 20%) mapped back
## to the original-model probability scale via the recalibration intercept, so
## that they sit correctly on the single ROC curve.
recal_threshold_pct <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.20)
standard_scale_thresholds <- plogis(qlogis(recal_threshold_pct) - new_intercept)
thresh_std <- get_threshold_points(roc_standard, standard_scale_thresholds,
                                     labels = sprintf("%.1f%%", recal_threshold_pct * 100))
print(thresh_std)

set.seed(2024)
ci_se_obj <- pROC::ci.se(roc_standard, specificities = seq(0, 1, 0.01), boot.n = 2000, progress = "none")
ci_se_df <- as.data.frame(unclass(ci_se_obj)) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("specificity") %>%
  mutate(specificity = as.numeric(specificity)) %>%
  rename(sens_lower = `2.5%`, sens_median = `50%`, sens_upper = `97.5%`)

## Ties in specificity are sorted by sensitivity so that vertical steps are
## drawn in the correct direction.
roc_line_df <- tibble(specificity = roc_standard$specificities, sensitivity = roc_standard$sensitivities) %>%
  arrange(desc(specificity), sensitivity)

roc_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = ci_se_df, aes(x = specificity, ymin = sens_lower, ymax = sens_upper),
              fill = PLOT_BLUE, alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_path(data = roc_line_df, aes(x = specificity, y = sensitivity), color = PLOT_BLUE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 1, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  geom_point(data = thresh_std, aes(x = specificity, y = sensitivity), color = "black", size = 2) +
  geom_text(data = thresh_std, aes(x = specificity, y = sensitivity, label = label), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  scale_x_reverse(limits = c(1, 0)) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(x = "Specificity", y = "Sensitivity") +
  theme_bw()

ggsave("results/figure_2_roc_curve.png", roc_plot, width = 6, height = 5, dpi = 300)

## ---- 16. Flow diagram ---------------------------------------------------------

build_flow_diagram <- function(flow_tbl, box_width = 1.05, box_height = 0.6, vgap = 1.05) {
  flow_tbl <- head(flow_tbl, -1)
  n_steps <- nrow(flow_tbl)
  flow_tbl$Step[n_steps] <- paste0(flow_tbl$Step[n_steps], "  ->  Final validation sample")

  seq_steps <- tibble(
    label = paste0(flow_tbl$Step, "\nN = ", format(flow_tbl$n_remaining, big.mark = ",")),
    y = rev(seq_len(n_steps)) * vgap
  )
  seq_excl <- tibble(
    y    = seq_steps$y[-n_steps] - box_height / 2,
    yend = seq_steps$y[-1] + box_height / 2,
    label = paste0("-", format(flow_tbl$n_excluded_this_step[-1], big.mark = ","))
  )

  ggplot() +
    geom_rect(data = seq_steps,
              aes(xmin = -box_width, xmax = box_width, ymin = y - box_height / 2, ymax = y + box_height / 2),
              fill = "white", color = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(data = seq_steps, aes(x = 0, y = y, label = label), size = 3.0, lineheight = 0.9) +
    geom_segment(data = seq_excl, aes(x = 0, xend = 0, y = y, yend = yend),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15, "cm"), type = "closed"), linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_text(data = seq_excl, aes(x = box_width + 0.15, y = (y + yend) / 2, label = label),
              size = 2.7, hjust = 0, color = "gray30") +
    xlim(-box_width - 0.3, box_width + 1.8) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(10, 90, 10, 10))
}

## build_flow_diagram() drops the last row of flow_table (mania data
## availability) and labels the row above as the final sample. This is valid
## only if nobody is excluded at that step, which is asserted here.
stopifnot(n_18y_outcome_available == n_final)
flow_diagram_plot <- build_flow_diagram(flow_table)
ggsave("results/figure_s1_flow_diagram.png", flow_diagram_plot, width = 9, height = 8.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

## ---- 17. Sensitivity: recoding of "no parental figure present" (Table S8) ----
## Every substantive category (great, very good, good, regular, bad [= main
## analysis]) and exclusion of these adolescents. This is separate from
## Sensitivities 1-4 below. Original (non-recalibrated) model only:
## recalibrating within each scenario would re-equalise mean predicted and
## observed risk and mask sensitivity to the coding choice.

apply_recode_scenario <- function(base_data, scenario = c("bad", "great", "very_good", "good", "regular", "exclude")) {
  scenario <- match.arg(scenario)
  if (scenario == "exclude") {
    return(base_data %>% filter(!(father_recoded_to_ref | mother_recoded_to_ref | between_recoded_to_ref)))
  }
  target_cat <- switch(scenario, great = 1, very_good = 2, good = 3, regular = 4, bad = 5)
  base_data %>%
    mutate(
      rel_mother_cat  = ifelse(mother_recoded_to_ref,  target_cat, rel_mother_cat),
      rel_father_cat  = ifelse(father_recoded_to_ref,  target_cat, rel_father_cat),
      rel_between_cat = ifelse(between_recoded_to_ref, target_cat, rel_between_cat)
    )
}

scenario_labels <- c(
  bad       = "Main analysis: recoded to \"bad\"",
  great     = "Sensitivity 1: recoded to \"great\"",
  very_good = "Sensitivity 2: recoded to \"very good\"",
  good      = "Sensitivity 3: recoded to \"good\"",
  regular   = "Sensitivity 4: recoded to \"regular\"",
  exclude   = "Sensitivity 5: excluded entirely"
)

pel_2004_valid_raw_rel <- pel_2004_valid %>%
  mutate(rel_mother_cat = rel_mother_raw, rel_father_cat = rel_father_raw, rel_between_cat = rel_between_raw)

## Bootstrap 95% CIs for every metric (unweighted).
sensitivity_results <- list()
for (scen in names(scenario_labels)) {
  scen_data  <- apply_recode_scenario(pel_2004_valid_raw_rel, scen)
  scen_model <- build_lp(scen_data)
  scen_metrics <- bootstrap_all_metrics(scen_model, "predicted_prob", "lp", n_boot = N_BOOT)
  sensitivity_results[[scen]] <- scen_metrics %>% mutate(Scenario = scenario_labels[scen], .before = 1)
}

sensitivity_table <- bind_rows(sensitivity_results) %>%
  transmute(
    Scenario, N = n, Events = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n_events, 100 * n_events / N),
    `C-statistic (95% CI)` = fmt_ci_boot(c_statistic, c_statistic_lo, c_statistic_hi),
    `Calibration slope (95% CI)` = fmt_ci_boot(cal_slope, cal_slope_lo, cal_slope_hi),
    `Calibration-in-the-large (95% CI)` = fmt_ci_boot(citl_logodds, citl_logodds_lo, citl_logodds_hi),
    `O/E ratio (95% CI)` = fmt_ci_boot(OE_ratio, OE_ratio_lo, OE_ratio_hi),
    `Brier score (95% CI)` = fmt_ci_boot(brier, brier_lo, brier_hi, 3)
  )
cat("\n--- Table S8 (parent-figure-recoding sensitivity) ---\n"); print(sensitivity_table, width = Inf)

## ---- 18. Linear predictor spread: 2004 vs. 1993 -----------------------------

lp_mean <- mean(pel_2004_model$lp, na.rm = TRUE)
lp_sd   <- sd(pel_2004_model$lp, na.rm = TRUE)
lp_median <- median(pel_2004_model$lp, na.rm = TRUE)
lp_q1 <- as.numeric(quantile(pel_2004_model$lp, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE))
lp_q3 <- as.numeric(quantile(pel_2004_model$lp, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE))

linear_predictor_comparison <- tibble(
  Cohort    = c("Pelotas 1993 (development, internal validation)", "Pelotas 2004 (this validation)"),
  Mean_lp   = c(-3.678, round(lp_mean, 3)),
  SD_lp     = c(0.685, round(lp_sd, 3)),
  Median_lp = c(NA_real_, round(lp_median, 3)),
  Q1_lp     = c(NA_real_, round(lp_q1, 3)),
  Q3_lp     = c(NA_real_, round(lp_q3, 3)),
  Source    = c("Rocha et al. (2021), Supplement 2", "This analysis")
)
cat("\n--- Linear predictor spread: 2004 vs. 1993 ---\n"); print(linear_predictor_comparison)

## ---- 19. Screening diagnostics for Sensitivities 2-4 (IQ, SDQ, DAWBA-11) ----

## fqiwiscstd is a Z-score in this sample (mean ~0, SD 1), not a deviation IQ
## (mean 100, SD 15), so IQ < 70 corresponds to Z < (70 - 100) / 15 = -2.0.
## Participants with missing IQ (mostly non-participation at the age-6 wave) are
## excluded, mirroring the 1993 requirement for a valid IQ measurement.
IQ_Z_CUTOFF <- -2.0
status_data <- status_data %>%
  mutate(iq6_missing = is.na(fqiwiscstd), iq6_excludes = iq6_missing | (fqiwiscstd < IQ_Z_CUTOFF))

## Standard five-item SDQ emotional-symptoms subscale (0/1/2 each). The cut-off
## of 4 follows Goodman's parent-report "borderline or abnormal" band (0-3 close
## to average, 4 borderline, 5-10 abnormal). Rocha et al. (2021) describe the
## 1993 rule only as a "borderline score" without a numeric cut-off, and SDQ
## norms in Brazilian samples differ from the UK bands; the cut-off flags more
## adolescents than expected under UK norms (see screening_diagnostics).
## Sensitivity 4 is therefore exploratory.
SDQ_BORDERLINE_CUTOFF <- 4
status_data <- status_data %>%
  mutate(
    sdq_emo_11_sum = p1somatic_11 + p1worries_11 + p1unhappy_11 + p1clingy_11 + p1afraid_11,
    sdq_emo_15_sum = p1somatic_15 + p1worries_15 + p1unhappy_15 + p1clingy_15 + p1afraid_15,
    sdq_emo_11_borderline = sdq_emo_11_sum >= SDQ_BORDERLINE_CUTOFF,
    sdq_emo_15_borderline = sdq_emo_15_sum >= SDQ_BORDERLINE_CUTOFF,
    ## Sensitivity 4: SDQ only (no DAWBA).
    baseline_depression_sdq_only = ifelse(
      !missing_15y_data,
      as.integer((sdq_emo_11_borderline %in% TRUE) | (sdq_emo_15_borderline %in% TRUE)),
      NA_integer_
    )
  )

## Same rule as the age-15 DAWBA fields (!= 0 is positive), applied to the
## age-11 fields. DAWBA-11 positivity is low, so it is a narrower,
## higher-specificity screen than the SDQ subscale.
status_data <- status_data %>%
  mutate(
    dawba15_positive = dcmadep != 0 | dcotdep != 0 | dcundif != 0 | icmadep != 0 | icotdep != 0 | icundif != 0,
    dawba11_positive = gdcmadep != 0 | gdcotdep != 0 | gdcundif != 0 | gicmadep != 0 | gicotdep != 0 | gicundif != 0,
    ## Sensitivity 3: DAWBA-15 or DAWBA-11 only (no SDQ).
    baseline_depression_dawba_only = ifelse(
      !missing_15y_data,
      as.integer((dawba15_positive %in% TRUE) | (dawba11_positive %in% TRUE)),
      NA_integer_
    )
  )

screening_diagnostics <- tibble(
  Metric = c("Missing IQ (age 6) data, full cohort",
             "IQ Z-score < -2.0 (IQ<70-equivalent), among those with IQ data",
             "SDQ emotional subscale >= cutoff at age 11, among those with 11y SDQ data",
             "SDQ emotional subscale >= cutoff at age 15, among those with 15y SDQ data",
             "DAWBA-11 positive (any of 6 fields), among those with 11y DAWBA data",
             "DAWBA-15 positive (any of 6 fields), among those with 15y DAWBA data"),
  n = c(sum(status_data$iq6_missing),
        sum(!status_data$iq6_missing & status_data$fqiwiscstd < IQ_Z_CUTOFF),
        sum(status_data$sdq_emo_11_borderline, na.rm = TRUE),
        sum(status_data$sdq_emo_15_borderline, na.rm = TRUE),
        sum(status_data$dawba11_positive, na.rm = TRUE),
        sum(status_data$dawba15_positive, na.rm = TRUE)),
  N_denominator = c(nrow(status_data), sum(!status_data$iq6_missing),
                     sum(!is.na(status_data$sdq_emo_11_sum)), sum(!is.na(status_data$sdq_emo_15_sum)),
                     sum(!is.na(status_data$gdcmadep)), sum(!is.na(status_data$dcmadep)))
) %>%
  mutate(Pct = round(100 * n / N_denominator, 1))
cat("\n--- Screening diagnostics (IQ, SDQ, DAWBA-11) ---\n"); print(screening_diagnostics, n = Inf)

## baseline_depression_sdq_only and baseline_depression_dawba_only treat a
## missing screen as screen-negative (%in% TRUE reads NA as FALSE) among
## participants with complete age-15 data. The extent is reported below.
missing_screen_as_negative <- tibble(
  Screen = c("SDQ emotional subscale, age 11", "SDQ emotional subscale, age 15", "DAWBA-11 (6 fields)"),
  N_missing_among_15y_complete = c(
    sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data & is.na(status_data$sdq_emo_11_sum)),
    sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data & is.na(status_data$sdq_emo_15_sum)),
    sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data & is.na(status_data$gdcmadep))
  ),
  N_15y_complete = sum(!status_data$missing_15y_data)
) %>%
  mutate(Pct = round(100 * N_missing_among_15y_complete / N_15y_complete, 1))
cat("\n--- Missing alternative baseline-depression screen, defaulted to screen-negative (Sensitivities 3/4) ---\n")
print(missing_screen_as_negative)

## ---- Sensitivity-sample builder -------------------------------------------
## Adds the IQ and/or alternative depression-screen criteria on top of all other
## main-analysis exclusions.

build_sensitivity_sample <- function(depression_col, apply_iq) {
  d <- status_data %>%
    mutate(
      baseline_depression_this = .data[[depression_col]],
      iq_ex_this = if (apply_iq) iq6_excludes else FALSE,
      eligibility_status_this = case_when(
        missing_15y_data                      ~ "Excluded: missing 15y predictor/baseline-diagnosis data",
        !(puberty_data_present %in% TRUE)     ~ "Excluded: missing puberty data",
        is.na(puberty_started)                ~ "Excluded: ambiguous puberty status",
        !(puberty_started %in% TRUE)          ~ "Excluded: pre-pubertal at 15y",
        iq_ex_this %in% TRUE                  ~ "Excluded: IQ<70-equivalent or missing IQ at 6y",
        baseline_depression_this == 1         ~ "Excluded: baseline depression (extended or standard screen)",
        missing_18y_outcome                   ~ "Excluded: missing 18y depression outcome",
        !(mania_data_present %in% TRUE)       ~ "Excluded: missing mania/hypomania screening data",
        TRUE                                    ~ "Included: valid case"
      )
    )
  final <- d %>% filter(eligibility_status_this == "Included: valid case")
  list(final_ids = final$idalt20241223, n_final = nrow(final))
}

## Built with build_analytic_dataset() rather than by filtering pel_2004_valid:
## the DAWBA-only and SDQ-only screens are not nested within the main screen, so
## a participant excluded from the main sample can qualify for a sensitivity
## sample, and vice versa.
build_sensitivity_model <- function(sens_ids) {
  built <- build_analytic_dataset(sens_ids) %>% filter(!is.na(depression_outcome))
  stopifnot(nrow(built) == length(sens_ids))
  built %>% build_lp()
}

## Full report for one sensitivity analysis: recalibration, bootstrap CIs
## (original and recalibrated), Table 2-style table, prevalence-gap
## decomposition and calibration plots.
report_sensitivity <- function(sens_label, model_data, n_boot = N_BOOT) {
  recal_model_s <- glm(depression_outcome ~ offset(lp), data = model_data, family = binomial)
  new_intercept_s <- unname(coef(recal_model_s)[1])
  model_data <- model_data %>%
    mutate(lp_recal = lp + new_intercept_s, predicted_prob_recal = 1 / (1 + exp(-lp_recal)))

  boot_std   <- bootstrap_all_metrics(model_data, "predicted_prob", "lp", n_boot = n_boot)
  boot_recal <- bootstrap_all_metrics(model_data, "predicted_prob_recal", "lp_recal", n_boot = n_boot)

  perf_table <- build_table2_style(boot_std, boot_recal)

  gap <- decompose_prevalence_gap(model_data$depression_outcome, model_data$predicted_prob) %>%
    mutate(Scenario = sens_label, .before = 1)

  cal_std   <- build_calibration_plot(model_data, "predicted_prob",       "depression_outcome", title = paste0(sens_label, " - Original model"))
  cal_recal <- build_calibration_plot(model_data, "predicted_prob_recal", "depression_outcome", title = paste0(sens_label, " - Recalibrated model"))

  cat(sprintf("\n--- %s ---\n", sens_label))
  cat(sprintf("N = %d | Observed prevalence = %.1f%% | Mean predicted risk = %.2f%% | Case-mix explains ~%.1f of the %.1f-point rise vs. 1993; residual ~%.1f points\n",
              nrow(model_data), gap$Observed_prevalence_pct, gap$Mean_predicted_risk_pct,
              gap$Casemix_explained_pct, gap$Total_gap_pct, gap$Residual_pct))
  print(perf_table, width = Inf)

  list(table = perf_table, gap = gap, boot_std = boot_std, boot_recal = boot_recal,
       cal_std = cal_std, cal_recal = cal_recal, new_intercept = new_intercept_s, model_data = model_data)
}

## ---- 20. Sensitivity 1: IPW re-weighting ------------------------------------
## Reweights the final sample and excludes nobody. Stage 1 models completion of
## the age-15 assessment (sex, skin colour, maternal education, household
## income); Stage 2 models availability of the age-18 outcome (the 11 IDEA-RS
## predictors).

status_data <- status_data %>%
  mutate(
    ## Observed and eligible at age 15. Used only for the descriptive comparison
    ## in Table S5, not as the Stage 1 outcome (see stage1_fit_data).
    reached_15y_eligible = as.integer(!missing_15y_data & baseline_depression == 0 & puberty_started %in% TRUE),
    aescmae4cat_imp = ifelse(is.na(aescmae4cat), 9, aescmae4cat)  ## 9 = "Missing" category
  )

## Stage 1 models attrition only: whether the age-15 assessment was completed
## with usable predictor and puberty data. Participants excluded by design
## (pre-pubertal, baseline depression) were observed at age 15, so coding them
## as failures would conflate an eligibility criterion with loss to follow-up;
## they are dropped from this fitting sample.
stage1_fit_data <- status_data %>%
  filter(eligibility_group != "Excluded (by design / eligibility criterion)") %>%
  mutate(observed_15y_eligible = as.integer(!missing_15y_data & (puberty_data_present %in% TRUE) & !is.na(puberty_started)))

## P(age-15 assessment completed with usable data | sex, skin colour, maternal
## education, household income). Missing maternal education is its own factor
## level, so every participant receives a Stage 1 probability. Household income
## (arendsm) enters continuous and untransformed, as a balancing covariate
## rather than an effect estimate. Sex is retained for consistency with Stage 2.
stage1_model <- glm(observed_15y_eligible ~ factor(asexo) + factor(acorpele) + factor(aescmae4cat_imp) + arendsm,
                     data = stage1_fit_data, family = binomial)
cat("\n--- IPW Stage 1 model: P(15y assessment completed with usable data | sex, skin colour, maternal education, household income) ---\n")
print(summary(stage1_model)$coefficients)

status_data <- status_data %>% mutate(stage1_prob = predict(stage1_model, newdata = ., type = "response"))
marginal_stage1 <- mean(stage1_fit_data$observed_15y_eligible)

## Stage 2: P(age-18 outcome observed | the 11 IDEA-RS predictors), fitted in
## the age-15-eligible sample. The full predictor set is used, rather than only
## predictors significantly associated with loss to follow-up, to avoid
## selecting covariates on the association the weights are meant to correct for.
eligible_15y_data <- eligible_15y_data %>% mutate(has_18y_outcome = as.integer(!missing_18y_outcome))
stage2_model <- glm(
  has_18y_outcome ~ factor(asexo) + factor(acorpele) + school_pos + drugs_pos + isolation_pos +
    fighting_pos + ranaway_pos + factor(maltreat_cat) + factor(rel_mother_cat) +
    factor(rel_father_cat) + factor(rel_between_cat),
  data = eligible_15y_data, family = binomial
)
cat("\n--- IPW Stage 2 model: P(18y outcome observed | 11 IDEA-RS predictors) ---\n")
print(summary(stage2_model)$coefficients)

eligible_15y_data <- eligible_15y_data %>% mutate(stage2_prob = predict(stage2_model, newdata = ., type = "response"))
marginal_stage2 <- mean(eligible_15y_data$has_18y_outcome)

attrition_weights <- status_data %>%
  transmute(subject_id = idalt20241223, stage1_prob) %>%
  inner_join(eligible_15y_data %>% transmute(subject_id = idalt20241223, stage2_prob),
             by = "subject_id", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(
    raw_ipw        = 1 / (stage1_prob * stage2_prob),
    stabilized_ipw = (marginal_stage1 / stage1_prob) * (marginal_stage2 / stage2_prob)
  )
stopifnot(nrow(attrition_weights) == n_15y_eligible)

summ_stats <- function(x) c(Min = min(x), Q1 = as.numeric(quantile(x, .25)), Median = median(x),
                             Mean = mean(x), Q3 = as.numeric(quantile(x, .75)), Max = max(x))
weight_diagnostics <- tibble(
  Statistic      = c("Min", "Q1", "Median", "Mean", "Q3", "Max"),
  Raw_IPW        = round(unname(summ_stats(attrition_weights$raw_ipw)), 3),
  Stabilized_IPW = round(unname(summ_stats(attrition_weights$stabilized_ipw)), 3)
)
cat("\n--- IPW weight diagnostics ---\n"); print(weight_diagnostics)

pel_2004_model_ipw <- pel_2004_model %>%
  inner_join(attrition_weights %>% select(subject_id, stabilized_ipw), by = "subject_id", relationship = "one-to-one")
stopifnot(nrow(pel_2004_model_ipw) == nrow(pel_2004_model))

## Weighted bootstrap for the IPW sensitivity analysis: each replicate resamples
## birth-cohort rows uniformly and refits both IPW stages, so the CIs reflect
## uncertainty in the weights as well as in the outcome model. Weighted metrics
## come from compute_weighted_validation_metrics(), evaluated once per
## replicate.
bootstrap_ipw_sensitivity <- function(master, prob_col, lp_col, n_boot = N_BOOT, seed = 2024) {
  set.seed(seed)
  n <- nrow(master)
  boot_list <- vector("list", n_boot)
  warn_env <- new.env(); warn_env$n <- 0
  for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    idx <- sample.int(n, size = n, replace = TRUE)
    rs  <- master[idx, ]
    boot_list[[b]] <- run_boot_replicate({
      m1 <- glm(observed_15y_eligible ~ factor(asexo) + factor(acorpele) + factor(aescmae4cat_imp) + arendsm,
                data = rs[rs$in_stage1_fit, ], family = binomial)
      m2 <- glm(
        has_18y_outcome ~ factor(asexo) + factor(acorpele) + school_pos + drugs_pos + isolation_pos +
          fighting_pos + ranaway_pos + factor(maltreat_cat) + factor(rel_mother_cat) +
          factor(rel_father_cat) + factor(rel_between_cat),
        data = rs[rs$in_stage2_fit, ], family = binomial
      )

      rs$stage1_prob_b <- predict(m1, newdata = rs, type = "response")
      marg1_b <- mean(rs$observed_15y_eligible[rs$in_stage1_fit])

      rs$stage2_prob_b <- NA_real_
      rs$stage2_prob_b[rs$in_stage2_fit] <- predict(m2, newdata = rs[rs$in_stage2_fit, ], type = "response")
      marg2_b <- mean(rs$has_18y_outcome[rs$in_stage2_fit])

      rs$stabilized_ipw_b <- (marg1_b / rs$stage1_prob_b) * (marg2_b / rs$stage2_prob_b)

      ars <- rs[!is.na(rs[[prob_col]]), ]
      compute_weighted_validation_metrics(ars$depression_outcome, ars[[prob_col]], ars[[lp_col]], ars$stabilized_ipw_b)
    }, warn_env)
  }
  n_failed <- sum(vapply(boot_list, is.null, logical(1)))
  if (n_failed > 0) cat(sprintf("  (IPW bootstrap: %d/%d replicates failed and were dropped)\n", n_failed, n_boot))
  if (warn_env$n > 0) cat(sprintf("  (IPW bootstrap: %d warnings raised across %d replicates)\n", warn_env$n, n_boot))
  boot_df <- bind_rows(boot_list)

  analytic <- master[!is.na(master[[prob_col]]), ]
  point <- compute_weighted_validation_metrics(analytic$depression_outcome, analytic[[prob_col]], analytic[[lp_col]], analytic$stabilized_ipw)

  out <- point
  for (m in BOOTSTRAP_METRIC_NAMES) {
    out[[paste0(m, "_lo")]] <- round(as.numeric(quantile(boot_df[[m]], 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)), 4)
    out[[paste0(m, "_hi")]] <- round(as.numeric(quantile(boot_df[[m]], 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)), 4)
  }
  out
}

## One row per birth-cohort member with every column needed to refit both IPW
## stages and evaluate the outcome model, so each bootstrap replicate resamples
## a single data frame.
ipw_master <- status_data %>%
  transmute(
    subject_id = idalt20241223,
    in_stage1_fit = eligibility_group != "Excluded (by design / eligibility criterion)",
    observed_15y_eligible = as.integer(!missing_15y_data & (puberty_data_present %in% TRUE) & !is.na(puberty_started)),
    in_stage2_fit = !missing_15y_data & baseline_depression == 0 & puberty_started %in% TRUE,
    has_18y_outcome = as.integer(!missing_18y_outcome),
    asexo, acorpele, aescmae4cat_imp, arendsm
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    eligible_15y_data %>%
      transmute(subject_id = idalt20241223, school_pos, drugs_pos, isolation_pos,
                fighting_pos, ranaway_pos, maltreat_cat, rel_mother_cat, rel_father_cat, rel_between_cat),
    by = "subject_id", relationship = "one-to-one"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    pel_2004_model_ipw %>% transmute(subject_id, depression_outcome, lp, predicted_prob, stabilized_ipw),
    by = "subject_id", relationship = "one-to-one"
  )
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ipw_master$subject_id), nrow(ipw_master) == nrow(status_data))

## Recalibration intercept for the IPW scenario, held fixed across replicates as
## in report_sensitivity(): the bootstrap re-estimates the weights, not the
## recalibration.
recal_model_ipw <- glm(depression_outcome ~ offset(lp), data = pel_2004_model_ipw, family = binomial,
                        weights = pel_2004_model_ipw$stabilized_ipw)
new_intercept_ipw <- unname(coef(recal_model_ipw)[1])
pel_2004_model_ipw <- pel_2004_model_ipw %>%
  mutate(lp_recal = lp + new_intercept_ipw, predicted_prob_recal = 1 / (1 + exp(-lp_recal)))
ipw_master <- ipw_master %>%
  left_join(pel_2004_model_ipw %>% transmute(subject_id, lp_recal, predicted_prob_recal),
            by = "subject_id", relationship = "one-to-one")
stopifnot(nrow(ipw_master) == nrow(status_data))

boot_std_ipw   <- bootstrap_ipw_sensitivity(ipw_master, "predicted_prob", "lp")
boot_recal_ipw <- bootstrap_ipw_sensitivity(ipw_master, "predicted_prob_recal", "lp_recal")
perf_table_ipw <- build_table2_style(boot_std_ipw, boot_recal_ipw)

gap_ipw <- decompose_prevalence_gap(pel_2004_model_ipw$depression_outcome, pel_2004_model_ipw$predicted_prob,
                                      weights = pel_2004_model_ipw$stabilized_ipw) %>%
  mutate(Scenario = "Sensitivity 1: IPW (maternal education + household income)", .before = 1)

cal_std_ipw   <- build_calibration_plot(pel_2004_model_ipw, "predicted_prob",       "depression_outcome",
                                          weight_col = "stabilized_ipw", title = "Sensitivity 1: IPW - Original model")
cal_recal_ipw <- build_calibration_plot(pel_2004_model_ipw, "predicted_prob_recal", "depression_outcome",
                                          weight_col = "stabilized_ipw", title = "Sensitivity 1: IPW - Recalibrated model")

cat("\n--- Sensitivity 1: IPW (maternal education + household income) ---\n")
cat(sprintf("N = %d | Observed prevalence = %.1f%% | Mean predicted risk = %.2f%% | Case-mix explains ~%.1f of the %.1f-point rise vs. 1993; residual ~%.1f points\n",
            nrow(pel_2004_model_ipw), gap_ipw$Observed_prevalence_pct, gap_ipw$Mean_predicted_risk_pct,
            gap_ipw$Casemix_explained_pct, gap_ipw$Total_gap_pct, gap_ipw$Residual_pct))
print(perf_table_ipw, width = Inf)

sens1_report <- list(table = perf_table_ipw, gap = gap_ipw, boot_std = boot_std_ipw, boot_recal = boot_recal_ipw,
                      cal_std = cal_std_ipw, cal_recal = cal_recal_ipw, new_intercept = new_intercept_ipw,
                      model_data = pel_2004_model_ipw)
```
